contract.behavior: Assess actual package mechanisms on predeclared cases without changing product policy.
contract.authority: Host owns schema, migration callbacks/version-store choice/query closures; package owns execution/save/rollback.
contract.ordering: Main-context MainActor; actor serial synchronous closures; migration checkpoint only after successful callback.
contract.envelopes: No built-in query/batch/input/time budget; workload bounds host-owned, unknown consumers. Exactly three sources and 34 pin pairs.
contract.failures: Typed DatabaseError preserved; generic read error fetchFailed; generic write error transactionFailed with rollback; generic migration error migrationFailed. Runtime outcomes unknown.
contract.claims: Membership is not caller or execution; async wrapper is not off-main evidence; callback runner is not SwiftData schema migration proof.

cases.supported: Reads version, returns unchanged when >= target; groups fromVersion, picks smallest toVersion, requires strictly increasing step; advances checkpoint only after callback returns. Missing/progress-invalid step throws.
cases.unknown: Host-provided chain constraints and actual app use.
cases.candidate: Public runner accepts an overshooting transition (0->5 at target2), executes it and returns5; duplicate/invalid smallest edge can block a valid alternative. Actual implementation fact; no shipped migration defect established.
cases.severity: conditional P2 if exact target ceiling is host contract; otherwise API clarification recommendation
cases.remedy: Before adopting, define producer constraints for unique progressive chain within target; reject invalid chain before irreversible callbacks if exact target intended.

cases.supported: Failure does not advance current version for failing callback. Prior successful step versions remain. No delete/reset operation in reviewed sources.
cases.unknown: Callback may commit data before failure; runner has no encompassing rollback, durable atomic checkpoint or crash shielding. UserDefaults checkpoint separate from database commit. Idempotence, failure/relaunch, actual schema/downgrade/disk-full/crash evidence not observed.
cases.recommendation: Host must provide idempotent/checkpointed callbacks and old-store failure/reopen evidence; do not label generic callback runner schema-safe.

cases.supported: Success returns only after save (actor conditional hasChanges). Typed and generic operation/save errors roll back context then throw. No automatic retry. Synchronous closure+save has no intervening actor await.
cases.unknown: Rollback only affects pending context state, not caller-owned files/network side effects or prior commits; unrelated pending main-context changes share rollback/save scope. Retry idempotence and real save failure not executed.
cases.recommendation: Bound transaction to owner context and atomic local changes; external effects need explicit host policy.

cases.supported: Typed SwiftData closure bridges to Any with checked cast; unsupported missing callback/context fails. Actor Result requires Sendable; main-context return stays MainActor.
cases.unknown: ModelContext is mutable and exposed to closure; read-only is caller contract, not capability enforcement. A mutating read can leave pending work or save directly; that is hypothetical misuse absent legitimate caller evidence. No automatic read rollback.
cases.recommendation: Use read closures for reads and immutable Sendable actor results/stable identifiers; no new wrapper justified without actual consumer pressure.

cases.supported: A CancellationError thrown by read becomes fetchFailed; by write becomes transactionFailed after rollback; by migration becomes migrationFailed. Typed DatabaseError remains typed. APIs never check task cancellation themselves; async wrappers invoke synchronous main-context work directly.
cases.classification: Confirmed public mechanism transforms cancellation taxonomy. Conditional P2 if callers require CancellationError propagation/no cancelled commit; no inspected shipping caller. Baseline recommends propagation; current docs do not promise cancellability.
cases.remedy: When cancellation contract is selected, preserve CancellationError after required rollback and choose explicit pre-operation/pre-save checks; do not invent retroactive cancellation of a durable commit.
cases.unknown: Caller task ownership, user-visible mapping, cancellation latency and scheduling; no runtime evidence.

cases.supported: MainActor is legitimate mainContext compatibility surface. Documentation warns against heavy work. Separate ModelActor context and Sendable actor returns; no unchecked Sendable or unsafe escape in three sources.
cases.unknown: Actor initializer executor, thread/main-queue placement, closure resource bounds and main/actor merge visibility. @ModelActor is isolation, not proof every operation runs off-main.
cases.recommendation: Keep main operations small; verify actual creation/workload path before declaring main-thread stall or background performance.

cases.evidence: package README/PackageContract/LOCAL_USE/USAGE; scoped PBX six memberships and two scheme files
cases.supported: All three sources declared in TchopApp and TchopAppOcean only. Package docs keep schema/migrations/product policy with host; no runtime or shipping invocation established. Error strings use String(describing:) (caller error contents unspecified).
cases.unknown: All actual callers, app lifecycle/UI/privacy/telemetry/schema and release claims; no log/export observed.
cases.recommendation: Do not infer production reachability, privacy leak, preservation/reopen or completed migration from compilation or current mandatory-plan fixture history.

Treat read-only as caller discipline, not immutable context guarantee.
Keep migration checkpoint durability/idempotence and actual SwiftData schema evolution evidence separate.
Clarify cancellation and error-string disclosure contracts before expanding affected APIs.
